tasks.short: Confer on curriculum-aligned lesson plans and timing

steps.what: Retrieve the approved curriculum, current lesson sequence and actual shared-room constraints in {LMS} and {DOCS}; configure native course views to reduce repeated navigation, checking versions and missing constraints with their owners.
Confer with other staff members to plan and schedule lessons promoting learning, following approved curricula; resolve sequencing, practical resources and teaching responsibilities together.

Write the agreed lesson sequence, dates, curriculum references and responsibilities in the shared {LMS} course plan; configure native curriculum references and reusable plan fields, then check the completed plan against the actual staff agreement.
Commit the checked final lesson plan and timing to the shared staff course plan in {LMS}.

tasks.design: Configure course views and reusable curriculum references in {LMS}. Keep the staff discussion and agreement, then reduce repeated plan-field assembly before the ordinary final check and separate commit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Staff can repeat curriculum lookup and reference entry around the planning discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: Native course views and plan fields can reuse controlled curriculum references.
tasks.still_hard: Agree on a coherent teaching sequence with real resource limits.
tasks.human_edge: Reconcile pedagogical choices and colleague responsibilities.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated preparation and plan entry; collaborative decisions remain.

evidence.claim: Native course views and curriculum references can reduce repeated planning lookup and field entry without deciding lesson sequence.

assumptions: Boundary is this teacher's preparation, actual planning discussion and shared course-plan entry. Colleague time is not claimed or transferred. This is specific lesson planning, excluded from the general committee meeting task 6636. Shares are illustrative.

Curriculum owner supplies goal codes, approved revision and prerequisites; course records and room owner supply actual sequence and constraints. Teacher verifies missing details in s1; colleagues establish agreement in s2. There is no free ready-made lesson plan.

Native views and references precede code. Only repeated navigation and reference entry lose time, not substantive reading, agreement, writing or checking. This stores agreed lesson timing in the course plan, not a room reservation or meeting invite. Those actions are not assumed or credited.
s3 contains the ordinary completed-plan check and no added self-approval labour. a1 binds that final plan; edits require rechecking. The same-system commit retains its actual effort.
research_questions: Which repeated references remain manual in the existing course plan?

already_counted.description: Source verification, discussion, retained plan writing/check and commit remain in s1-s4.

incremental.description: Refresh curriculum links and reusable plan fields.

approvals.approved_version: Final agreed lesson sequence, dates and responsibilities checked in s3

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 9.3 less 1.5 upkeep gives 7.8. Upper range 7.5 removes repeated navigation and reference entry; zero if already configured.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Attend professional meetings, educational conferences and teacher training workshops, participate in actual exercises and discussions and evaluate what applies to middle-school career and technical education.

Write the actual professional-development reflection and completion details in the existing staff development record {OTHER}, checking the completed entry against actual participation and any issued attendance evidence.
Commit the checked development entry in the existing staff development record {OTHER} after the event actually occurs.

tasks.design: Retain actual professional participation and the separate existing development record in {OTHER}. Native record functions already handle the entry; no new automation or saving is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Learning and professional exchange require actual participation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing development-record entry is sufficient; no new enabler is claimed.
tasks.still_hard: Turn an event's ideas into useful teaching judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Question examples and learn from colleagues' experience.

ambition.what: No new service or decision rights.

tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in professional learning duties.

reach.learn: Transfer of training into classroom practice

evidence.claim: An existing development record can store actual attendance and reflection without replacing professional learning.

assumptions: Boundary starts at participation in an already confirmed event and includes the teacher's normal development record. Event selection, purchasing and registration are separate prior work and receive no saving here. Shares are illustrative for a teacher who keeps this existing record.

Event organiser supplies title, date and issued attendance evidence; teacher supplies actual participation and reflection in s1-s2. Missing evidence requires direct verification in s2, not inference from a calendar entry or scheduled end time. Unverified completion stays unverified.

Native record functions were considered. After separating the actual completion/reflection write and save from attendance, no removable duplicate work was found. Same-system saving retains full time. s2 is the ordinary final-entry check, not added approval time; edits invalidate the gate. No change means zero incremental upkeep.
research_questions: Is there genuine duplicate development entry beyond the current native record?

already_counted.description: Actual participation, reflection/completion entry and commit remain in s1-s3.

approvals.approved_version: Actual completed development entry checked after participation in s2

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Actual attendance and the separate existing record write/save remain fully counted, with no changed manual action.

tasks.short: Attend staff meetings and serve on committees

steps.what: Locate the current staff meeting agenda, committee papers and previous actions in {DOCS}; configure native meeting folders and version links to reduce repeated navigation while checking that the complete current pack is present.
Read the actual staff meeting and committee papers, consider their implications and prepare the teacher's substantive contribution and questions.
Attend staff meetings and serve on committees as required, discuss issues, challenge proposals and agree the teacher's own commitments with the other participants.
Write the teacher's assigned contribution and actual action commitments in the shared committee record {DOCS}, then check the completed content against the discussion and agreed responsibilities.
Commit the checked contribution and commitments in the shared committee record {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Configure native meeting-pack links in {DOCS}. Reduce repeated paper retrieval while retaining substantive reading, committee participation and the actual written contribution.
tasks.previous_blocker: Meeting papers and prior actions can be scattered across folders.
tasks.enabler_now: Native folder and version links can expose the current pack.
tasks.still_hard: Agree on workable commitments and question a weak proposal.
tasks.human_edge: Bring direct classroom experience to collective decisions.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less pack retrieval; committee work remains.

evidence.claim: Native document links can reduce repeated meeting-pack navigation without replacing substantive reading or committee contribution.

assumptions: Boundary is general staff/committee participation and the teacher's own assigned contribution, not secretary labour or the specific lesson-planning discussion in task 6634. Shares are illustrative; colleagues' work is neither claimed nor transferred.

Meeting owner supplies agenda version, paper IDs, current links and previous action references. Teacher verifies completeness in s1, reads them in s2 and produces actual commitments in s3-s4. Missing papers require normal source retrieval and clarification in s1; no generated meeting summary is assumed.

Native links precede code. Only repeated pack navigation loses time; substantive reading, discussion, actual writing and save remain. s4 contains the ordinary complete-contribution check, not an extra self-approval activity. Edits invalidate the requested commit gate.
research_questions: Are meeting papers already available through a single current pack?

already_counted.description: Retained retrieval, reading, meeting service, actual contribution and commit remain in s1-s5.

incremental.description: Check current-pack links and resolve moved references.

approvals.approved_version: Final assigned contribution and actual commitments checked in s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 3 less 0.5 upkeep gives 2.5. Zero if the pack is already directly linked; upper case removes navigation only.

steps.what: Plan the club, student organisation or academic contest with students, choosing suitable activities, responsibilities and supervision within the existing school arrangements.

Coordinate the activity time against actual staff, student and allocated-room availability using {CALENDAR}; configure native availability views to reduce repeated diary comparison, resolving missing responses and conflicts directly.

Prepare the activity notice in {LMS}; configure native date, location and contact fields from verified arrangements, then check the complete final notice, recipients, supervision details and required consent instructions.
outputs: checked final activity notice and audience

steps.what: Send the checked final activity notice to its verified student and guardian audience through the existing {LMS} communication channel.
inputs: checked final activity notice and audience

steps.what: Sponsor extracurricular activities through actual student mentoring, checking required permissions, supervision and practical coordination during the club or contest, handling questions and unexpected situations directly.
Record the actual attendance and any required factual activity note in the existing activity record {LMS}, then check the completed entry against what actually occurred.
Commit the checked actual activity entry in {LMS}.

tasks.design: Configure native availability views in {CALENDAR} and repeated notice fields in {LMS}. Keep planning, permission checks, student supervision and actual attendance recording; notice delivery and record commit stay separate gated actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coordination can repeat diary comparisons and standard notice fields.
tasks.enabler_now: Native availability views and notice templates can reuse explicit arrangements.
tasks.still_hard: Support students and respond to real supervision needs.
tasks.human_edge: Mentor students through shared extracurricular work.

ambition.what: No expanded participation or consent authority.

tasks.altitude: Less routine coordination while actual sponsorship remains.

reach.role: Teaching Assistants, Preschool, Elementary, Middle, and Secondary School, Except Special Education
reach.learn: Clear responsibilities and factual participation records

evidence.claim: Native availability views and notice fields can reduce repeated activity coordination without replacing permission checks or supervision.

assumptions: Boundary is an existing on-site activity using its already allocated room, not a new trip, external contest registration or booking transaction. Shares are illustrative; no saving or free transfer of room allocation or guardian work is claimed.

Teacher and students establish the actual plan in s1. Staff and room owners provide availability/constraints verified in s2, including direct follow-up. School policy supplies consent instructions; actual permissions are checked in s5, not inferred from silence. Missing fields or responses require manual clarification counted in s2 and s5.

Native views and templates precede code. Only repeated diary comparison and notice-field copying lose time. Supervision, actual writing of factual attendance and same-system sends/saves keep full effort.

s3 checks the completed notice and audience before sending; s6 checks the completed actual record after the activity occurs. These are ordinary checks, not extra self-approval work. Any content or recipient edit voids its corresponding gate.
research_questions: Which diary and notice fields are genuinely repeated today?

already_counted.description: Planning, retained coordination and notice checks, sending, supervision and actual record/commit remain in s1-s7.

incremental.description: Maintain notice fields and verify availability-view coverage.

approvals.approved_version: Final activity notice, consent instructions and audience checked in s3
Final actual activity entry checked after participation in s6

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 7.8 less 1 upkeep gives 6.8. Upper range 6.5 reduces repeated diary comparison and field copying; zero if native coordination is already configured.
